report:
MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Ax DWI B800, Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (mm2/s), Screen Save



> Wearing of articular cartilage and spur formation and subchondral edema, more severe at medial compartment, and in favor of loose bodies, reflecting osteoarthritis.
> There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, it extends into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Lateral meniscus appears to be normal.
> The contour of ACL & PCL MCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Slight interstitial increased singal of proximal LCL, R/O tendinosis
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. mild deep infrapatellar bursitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion with internal septums in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 2*2.5*6 cm in size ; mild perifocal edmea
> Mild fat stranding over infrapatellar fat pad.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee.
2. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. C/W Baker's cyst with perifocal edema.
4. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar plica.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda.
Hallazgos:
Edema óseo con fracturas trabeculares y corticales de la región central y posterior de platillo tibial lateral con
compromiso articular, sin desplazamiento ni hundimiento significativo. Existe compromiso parcial de la
eminencia intercondílea de la tibia, sin compromiso cortical regional.
No hay otras alteraciones de señal de la médula ósea.
Adelgazamiento y aumento de señal difuso del LCA. LCP y ligamentos colaterales sin alteraciones
significativas.
Irregularidad marginal del cuerpo y parte del cuerno posterior del menisco medial.
Menisco lateral de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial. El
resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Condropatía rotuliana
superficial difusa.
Leve derrame articular. Edema las partes blandas en la región posterolateral de la rodilla, probablemente
secundaria lesión capsular. Principales estructuras de la esquina posterolateral de la rodilla sin alteraciones.
Aumento de señal de la inserción proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Tendón cuadricipital,
tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Edema óseo fracturas trabeculares y corticales en la región central y posterior de platillo tibial lateral con
compromiso articular, sin hundimiento significativa.
Adelgazamiento y aumento de señal difuso del LCA, correlacionar con estabilidad clínica.
Fibrilación marginal del menisco medial.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 2 de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial y de la
rótula.
Leve derrame articular. Edema de la región poplítea la región posterolateral.
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal.

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion. There is a horizontal tear through the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral cartilage is preserved. Focal degeneration of the patellar ridge articular cartilage is noted with mild underlying bony change.  
Conclusion: Medial meniscal tear. Patellar ridge articular cartilage degeneration.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact There is no tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact The popliteofibular ligament is intact The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.Normal MR examination of the left knee.  Specifically, there is no evidence of meniscal, ligamentous, or articular cartilage abnormality.

There is bone contusion at the mid lateral femoral condyle and posterior lateral proximal tibia. 
    
  Hyperintense signal replaced entire of the ACL is observed.  Anterior tibial translation is noted. 
 Mild buckling PCL with intact ligament is seen. 
   
   Mild hyperintense proximal FCL is noted.   Popliteus and biceps femoris are preserved.  
 Small vertical tear at the meniscal body and radial tear at posterior horn and tear posterior root of the lateral meniscus are detected.    Edematous change of the popliteus muscle with fluid lesion, about intact9x1.9cm. intervening muscle fibers at the myotendinous junction, suggesting previous MTJ sprain. 
  
  Mild hyperintense deep MCL. 
  Horizontal tear meniscal body with massive radial tear involved posterior horn and posterior root of the  medial meniscus are noted.  
   
 Thinning articular cartilage along the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau with focal subchondral bone edema observed.  
  
 PF joint is intact.    
 MInimal joint effusion, with suprapatellar bursal fluid with mild thickened synovial tissue are observed.  -  Complete tear of ACL. 
  -  Mild FCL sprain, popliteus tendon and popliteus MTJ strain with focal cyst. 
  -  Small vertical tear at the meniscal body and radial tear at posterior horn and tear posterior root of the lateral meniscus  
  -  Radial torn posterior horn and tear posterior root of the lateral meniscus 
  -  Mild MCL sprain 
  -  Horizontal tear meniscal body with massive radial tear involved posterior horn and posterior root of the  medial meniscus 
 - Degenerative chondrosis of the medial tibiofemoral joint

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage without superimposed focal high-grade cartilage defects. Trochlear cartilage remains intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Findings predisposing to patellofemoral maltracking with impingement of superolateral Hoffa's fat. Otherwise normal MRI of the right knee.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia anterior rodilla izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior de ambos meniscos que no impresiona contactar
con la superficie articular, sin caracteres propios de rotura.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales de
predominio en el platillo tibial lateral.
Cartílago troclear sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales de espesor total de distribución difusa de la
rótula con cambios óseos secundarios. Edema el paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital
suprarrotuliano. Discreto edema del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Leve engrosamiento y aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la
inserción proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Leve derrame articular. Quiste poplíteo con fenómenos de filtración hacia caudal.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Condropatía lesiones grado dos de los compartimentos femorotibiales, predominando el platillo
tibial lateral.
Condropatía lesiones grado 4 de la rótula de extensión difusa.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal y cuadricipital distal.
Edema el paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano asociada signos de un síndrome de
hiperpresión externa de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular. Quiste poplíteo con fenómenos de filtración
